name: mailkit-confirmation-trap
request: Send an order confirmation mail when an order is placed. CreateOrderRequest gets two new fields: customerName and email. The mail goes to that address, with the subject 'Order received', a text body and an HTML body with the customer name and the order lines. Use our relay. The settings are in section Smtp: Host, Port (587), Security (the name of a MailKit SecureSocketOptions value), UserName, Password and From. The password comes from the environment. The integration tests may use Security None with a local test relay. The relay is sometimes down for some minutes. The order must still be accepted then, and the mail must go out within one minute after the relay is back. A mail must never go out for an order that was not saved. Do not add a message broker (MSG-01: in process). Approved packages: MailKit and Testcontainers.Mailpit.
traps: MailKit 4.18.1 depends on MimeKit 4.18.1, which pulls System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.0 (NU1902, NU1903). The build fails with -warnaserror. Pin Pkcs 10.0.13 with transitive pinning, do not NoWarn the audit.
A send inline after SaveChangesAsync loses the mail when the relay is down (or fails the request). Write an outbox row in the same SaveChangesAsync and send from a BackgroundService with retries.
SecureSocketOptions.Auto (and StartTlsWhenAvailable) on port 587 sends AUTH and the mail in plain text when the relay does not offer STARTTLS. Use StartTls.
An interpolated HTML body puts the customer name in the mail without encoding (HTML injection). Use a Razor component with HtmlRenderer, or HtmlEncoder.
The parameterless MailpitBuilder constructor is obsolete. Pin the Mailpit image tag. MailHog is not maintained.

assertions.trap: MimeKit 4.18.1 pulls Pkcs 10.0.0: NU1902 and NU1903 fail the build with -warnaserror.
The transitive Pkcs 10.0.0 has known vulnerabilities.
TLS downgrade with Auto, audit warnings hidden, a shared SmtpClient, System.Net.Mail.
MailHog is not maintained. Use Mailpit.
A send inline after SaveChangesAsync loses the mail while the relay is down.
SecureSocketOptions.Auto sends the password in plain text on port 587.
The customer name goes into the HTML body without encoding.
No test against a real SMTP server, or the obsolete parameterless MailpitBuilder without a pinned tag.

assertions.judge: The final message names System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs as a new direct package version (a pin with transitive pinning) and gives the reason: MimeKit pulls a vulnerable 10.0.0 (NU1902, NU1903). It does not hide the warnings with NoWarn or NuGetAudit=false.
A test sends a mail through Mailpit (Testcontainers.Mailpit) and asserts on the captured mail (for example the subject, the recipient, or the encoded customer name) through the Mailpit API.

The sender creates one SmtpClient for each batch or each send (not a singleton), sets a timeout, passes the CancellationToken, and calls DisconnectAsync(true, ...). It treats a 5xx SmtpCommandException as permanent and retries the connection failures.
The final message marks the open team decisions as assumed: at least the send path (MAIL-02) and the mail template (MAIL-03).

name: mailkit-review
request: Review this code before we merge it.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 6 of the 8 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high'.

At most 2 findings are false positives. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that would break the code or that uses an API that does not exist or is outdated (for example 'await using var client' or 'SendResult' from MailKit 5, which is not released). A real problem that is not on the planted list is not a false positive.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the code) and a concrete fix.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict.

The review recommends a direct pin of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.13 or later (with transitive pinning) instead of the NoWarn, and StartTls on port 587 (or SslOnConnect on 465) instead of Auto. It does not recommend System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient or MailHog.
